class.name: CaveNetwork3D
class.brief_description: Grows cave networks into the rock under a [TerrainGenerator3D], from entrances at cliff feet.
class.description: Each cave follows Paris, Peytavie, Guérin, Collon and Galin, "Synthesizing Geologically Coherent Cave Networks" (Computer Graphics Forum 40(7), 2021). Its key points are the entrance and sinks under closed hollows on the ground above. Points are sampled in the rock, more densely on the bedding planes and the water table, and joined to their nearest neighbours. Each edge costs the line integral of the medium: low along a bedding plane, a joint plane or the water table, low straight up or level, high when inclined. The least-cost paths between key points are kept by a gamma-skeleton. Side passages branch off as dead ends, every chain wanders by [member tortuosity], and some junctions open into breakdown chambers. Each passage takes a type from its height above the water table: a tube or bedding-plane passage at or below it, a keyhole just above it, a canyon well above it, and a shaft where it goes straight down. [method build_meshes] turns the caves into meshes. The rock round the passages is one distance field: each passage's section is swept along it and the passages are joined with a smooth minimum, chambers are ellipsoids with a breakdown floor, and the walls are roughened by noise. Within [member patch_radius] of an entrance the field also holds the ground, as Paris et al. carve a cave out of the terrain's own field. The field is polygonised per 16 m chunk by surface nets (Gibson 1998), with collision. Round each entrance a square patch carries the ground itself, drawn with [member ground_material], so the cliff, the opening and the passage are one surface. The [member generator] gets a hole 1.5 m inside that square, which [Landscape3D] (and a Terrain3D through [member RockField3D.terrain3d]) leaves out. Stones and plants already skip holes.

method.name: add_cave
method.description: Grows a cave from [param entrance] (the mouth's floor at the cliff foot) into the rock behind it ([param out] points away from the cliff). Returns its index, or -1 when there is too little rock behind the entrance. The same entrance and [member seed] always give the same cave.

method.name: add_sea_cave
method.description: Adds a sea cave at [param entrance] (a cliff foot at the sea, as [method find_sea_entrances] gives), opening toward [param out]. Waves quarry sea caves along a joint at the cliff foot (Moore 1954, Trenhaile). The passage runs straight along the joint for 35 to 95 m. It is a tall arch ([constant PASSAGE_SEA]), widest at the mouth, and its floor lies 1.5 m below the sea at the mouth and rises to high water at the back. Half of them end in a chamber. Where the chamber's roof is under 25 m thick, a shaft breaks through to the ground as a blowhole ([method get_blowholes]), and the terrain gets a hole there. Returns the cave's index, or -1 if the cliff behind is too thin.

method.name: build_meshes
method.description: Meshes the chunks of every cave that [param area] reaches, on worker threads, with collision when [member collision] is on, and opens the landscape over each entrance's patch. Returns how many chunks were made. Chunks already built are kept.

method.name: clear_caves
method.description: Forgets every cave.

method.name: clear_meshes
method.description: Frees every meshed chunk.

method.name: find_entrances
method.description: Cliff feet inside [param rect] where a cave could open. A foot qualifies when a wall of 50 to 76 degrees rises at least 8 m within 12 m of level ground with no water. When [member rock_field] is set, the rock there must also be limestone. Entrances are at least 150 m apart, steepest walls first, and at most [param max] are returned. Each is a [Dictionary] with [code]position[/code] (the mouth's floor) and [code]out[/code] (away from the cliff).

method.name: find_sea_entrances
method.description: Finds sea cave mouths in [param rect] (global x, z): cliffs at least 6 m over the sea, with water 0.3 to 30 m deep in front of them, a cliff foot within 8 m of the waterline and the ground between under high-water swash (0.6 m over the sea), so the sea reaches the mouth floor, and a steep rise to at least 6 m within 6 to 25 m behind the mouth. The mouths are at least 80 m apart and the tallest cliffs come first. Each entry is a [Dictionary] with [code]position[/code] (at sea level) and [code]out[/code] (toward the sea). Returns nothing without a sea.

method.name: get_blowholes
method.description: Where a sea cave's shaft opens at the ground (the terrain has a hole there).

method.name: get_cave_count
method.description: How many caves have been grown.

method.name: get_chambers
method.description: The cave's breakdown chambers. Each is a [Dictionary] with [code]center[/code], [code]radii[/code] (x and z across, y up) and [code]yaw[/code].

method.name: get_key_points
method.description: The cave's key points: the start of its passage behind the entrance, then its sinks.

method.name: get_last_build_msec
method.description: How long the last [method add_cave] took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_last_mesh_msec
method.description: How long the last [method build_meshes] took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_last_sample_count
method.description: How many points in the rock the last cave was grown through.

method.name: get_mesh_chunk_count
method.description: How many chunks are meshed.

method.name: is_streaming
method.description: Whether a batch of chunks for [member follow_target] is being meshed on worker threads.

method.name: get_mesh_triangle_count
method.description: Triangles in all the meshed chunks.

method.name: get_rock_distance
method.description: The distance field the meshes are made from, at [param position]: positive in the rock, negative in the open (in a passage or above the ground).

method.name: get_segments
method.description: The cave's passages as straight pieces. Each is a [Dictionary] with [code]a[/code], [code]b[/code], [code]radius_a[/code], [code]radius_b[/code] (half widths in metres) and [code]type[/code] (a [enum PassageType]).

method.name: get_rimstone_pool_count
method.description: How many rimstone pools the meshed chunks hold.

method.name: get_rimstone_pools
method.description: Each meshed rimstone pool as a [Dictionary]: [code]center[/code] (its water level in y), [code]depth[/code] (metres) and [code]outline[/code] (a [PackedVector2Array] of x and z round the center).

method.name: get_rimstone_water_count
method.description: How many pools have live water now (the ones nearest the camera, see [member rimstone_water_max]).

method.name: get_sea_mist_node
method.description: The network's own sea-mist node (see [member sea_mist]), or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_stream_count
method.description: How many cave streams ([member cave_streams]) are in the tree.

method.name: get_speleothem_count
method.description: How many stalactites, stalagmites and columns the meshed chunks hold.

method.name: is_sea_cave
method.description: Whether the cave was added with [method add_sea_cave].

members.member: Metres between the inception horizons: the bedding planes that passages favour. One passes through the entrance. They dip as the generator's strata do (else 1 to 4 degrees), wandering by a metre or two.
How far behind the entrance the network may reach, in metres.
The share of junctions that open into a breakdown chamber, 4 to 12 m across and kept under its cover of rock.
Each meshed chunk gets a static body with its triangles (backface collision on).
The least rock over a passage, in metres. It grows by 0.08 m per metre from the entrance, up to 15 m more.

A [Node3D] (usually the camera or the player) to stream meshes round. Chunks within [member stream_radius] are meshed on worker threads without stalling a frame, nearest first, when the target has moved 4 m; chunks further than the radius plus about two chunks are freed. Each entrance's patch chunks stay, since the landscape is open over the patch from any distance. Empty: no streaming ([method build_meshes] only).
The gamma-skeleton's exponent. Two key points are linked unless a third lies in their lune. 2 gives branchwork caves (the Gabriel graph). Lower values link more pairs, toward mazes.
The [TerrainGenerator3D] whose ground the caves lie under.

The material of an entrance patch's ground: the landscape's own (a TerrainMaterial3D works on any mesh), so the patch matches the cliff round it. When it has a [code]tm_rock_color[/code], the default wall material takes it too.
The surface nets cell in metres, rounded so a 16 m chunk holds whole cells.
Half the side of the square round each entrance where the meshes carry the ground and the landscape is opened (1.5 m less, so the two overlap). 0 for no patch.
An optional [RockField3D] that says what the rock is: [method find_entrances] then keeps to limestone.

How often a standing formation on a floor falling 2 to 20 degrees has a rimstone cascade below it. A cascade is 2 to 6 pools stepping down the fall line, each held by a sinuous dam with a level crest at the pool's spill level (Hammer, Dysthe, Jamtveit et al. 2007, 2010). Steeper floors give lower, closer dams. The dams are real geometry and the pool floors are coloured as calcite. 0: none.

Still water in the rimstone pools nearest the camera: a [code]PhysXWaterSurface3D[/code] cut to each pool's outline, with no sky reflection or caustics underground, stepped once per frame. Without the PhysX module the water is a plain sheet.
How many of the nearest pools have live water. Each one is a ripple simulation of its own.
How far from the camera pools have live water, in metres.
How rough the walls are: noise at 2.2 m (dissolution hollows) and 0.7 m (spalls), up to 0.35 m and 0.12 m at 1.
Metres between the points sampled in the rock. Smaller spacing gives finer paths and a slower build.

Dissolution scallops on the walls: dish-shaped hollows about 1.2 m across with sharp ridges between them, from Worley (cellular) noise. Real scallops are cells of this kind (Curl 1974), and these are the large ones that slow phreatic flow leaves. 0 turns them off.

Streams down the trench floors of the vadose passages (keyhole and canyon runs at least 8 m long, about two in three of them; the rest are dry): a channel cut into the fill and a [PhysXRiver3D] in it, run downhill to where the passage meets the water table. Needs the PhysX module.
When the network has sea caves, it makes its own [code]PhysXCaveMist3D[/code] (with the PhysX module built with Flow), which breathes cold mist out of their mouths with the swell.
The seed. Each cave also takes its entrance's position into its own seed.
How many dead-end side passages are tried, each joined to the network by its least-cost path.

How dense the drip formations are, which are instanced meshes in each chunk. A drip point is a roof facing down with a free fall under it, more of them where the rock above is thin, and none within 14 m of the entrance (Franke and Müller 2022). Each drip point gets a stalactite and usually a stalagmite under it, and a column where the two would meet. Lengths follow a power law. 0: none.
How far round [member follow_target] chunks are meshed, in metres.
How far passages wander off their paths: from a few centimetres at 0 to 4 m at 1.
The material of the passage walls. Without one, a built-in limestone in world space: mottled, with faint beds, darker and wet toward the floor, and the sediment floor brown.

constants.constant: The first metres from the mouth in.
Phreatic tube, round to elliptical, at or below the water table.
Phreatic passage along a bedding plane, wide and low.
A tube with a vadose trench cut in its floor, just above the water table.
Vadose canyon, tall and narrow, well above the water table.
A sea cave: a tall arch along a joint, floored below low water.
